implementation_notes: In .NET the god object is usually reachable through the container: a single `AddSingleton` of an `ApplicationContext`-style type whose constructor takes every repository, every client and every options object, injected via constructor everywhere. Microsoft's own dependency-injection guidance is the counter-move — constructor injection of narrow interfaces rather than a container-held god object, and `IServiceCollection` registrations scoped as narrowly as the lifetime really is. `partial class` is the specific trap: it lets a 3000-line class be split across several files, so the file-size smell disappears while the god object is entirely intact. Detect by counting constructor parameters and registered dependencies per type, not by lines.
idiom_name: ApplicationContext / Manager class plus DI container registration
pitfalls: `partial` hides size but not reach; split by responsibility, not by file.
Field injection (`[Inject] private IRepo _repo;`) hides dependencies from the constructor and makes the split invisible to both humans and tests.
A god object registered as a singleton is un-substitutable in every test that touches it, because the container hands out the same instance for the whole suite.
